case.case_title: Jayawardena v. Dharani Wijayatilake, Secretary, Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application 186/95, decided on 14 July 1995

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the cancellation of the petitioner's appointment as Inquirer into Sudden Deaths and the appointment of the 3rd respondent infringed the petitioner's fundamental rights under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his appointment was valid until 30.11.1996 and that the cancellation by the 1st respondent was without legal authority, without cause, and without a hearing, thus violating Article 12(1). He claimed the appointment of the 3rd respondent was also a nullity and that the actions were arbitrary, discriminatory, and politically motivated.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the petitioner's original appointment was flawed due to ineligibility at the time of application, that the cancellation was a rectification of a wrong appointment, and that no hearing was necessary. They argued the 1st respondent acted on ministerial or deputy ministerial directions and that the appointment of the 3rd respondent was valid.
key_facts: Petitioner was appointed Inquirer in 1990 and reappointed in 1993 for three years.
Petitioner's appointment was cancelled by the 1st respondent's letter dated 26.5.1995 without prior notice or hearing.
The 3rd respondent was appointed as Inquirer effective 1.6.1995 without advertisement or interview.
Petitioner was not informed of allegations or given opportunity to defend.
The 1st respondent had no legal authority to cancel the appointment; cancellation was illegal and a nullity.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 12(1) guarantees equal protection of the law, which includes protection against arbitrary removal from public office without cause and without due process. The office of Inquirer is public in nature and not held at pleasure, so termination requires cause and a hearing. The cancellation without notice or hearing violated principles of natural justice and thus denied the petitioner equal protection under the law.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was removed without any inquiry or opportunity to be heard, and the cancellation was effected by an official without legal authority. The appointment of the 3rd respondent without advertisement or interview further demonstrated arbitrariness. The court found the cancellation and new appointment illegal and null, constituting a violation of Article 12(1).
principles_established: Public office holders not stated to hold office at pleasure cannot be removed without cause and hearing.
Natural justice requires notice and opportunity to be heard before removal.
Arbitrary administrative decisions denying fair procedure violate equal protection of the law.
Illegal cancellation of appointment and subsequent appointment without due process are null and void.

outcome.holding: The court held that the cancellation of the petitioner's appointment and the appointment of the 3rd respondent infringed the petitioner's fundamental right under Article 12(1). The cancellation and appointment were illegal and null and void, and were quashed. The petitioner was entitled to function as Inquirer until 30.11.1996. Compensation and costs were awarded.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The cancellation and appointment were quashed; petitioner restored to office until 30.11.1996; Rs 25,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 costs awarded payable by the State.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court's reasoning as it guarantees equal protection of the law, which the petitioner argued was violated by arbitrary cancellation of his appointment without cause or hearing. The court's holding directly relied on this clause to find a fundamental rights violation.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was removed without cause or hearing by a letter from the 1st respondent who had no legal authority to cancel the appointment; the appointment of the 3rd respondent was made without advertisement or interview; the court found this violated Article 12(1).
